The map operations `containsKey`, `get`, and `put` can throw several runtime exceptions: `NullPointerException` (if `label` is null and the map does not allow null keys), `ClassCastException` (if the map requires keys to be comparable and `LabelNode` does not satisfy that requirement), `UnsupportedOperationException` (if the map is unmodifiable), and `IllegalArgumentException` (if the map imposes restrictions on keys/values). The method does not include any exception handling for these runtime exceptions. Although runtime exceptions are typically not required to be caught, the lack of handling could lead to unclear error messages or abrupt termination. Therefore, it is advisable to catch the most likely exceptions (e.g., `NullPointerException`, `ClassCastException`, `UnsupportedOperationException`) and rethrow them as more informative exceptions, such as `IllegalArgumentException`, to improve robustness and debuggability. A single try-catch structure can be added around the entire body of the method to achieve this.
